items: Continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) monitor gases such as CO, O3, SO2, NO2, VOCs and PM at industrial sites.
Air quality monitoring stations (AQMS): fixed stations with sensors and analysers that measure pollutant levels in real time, located in urban areas and industrial zones.
Remote sensing: satellites with sensors measure atmospheric pollutants over large areas, giving data on regional and global air quality.

blocks.prompt: What type of data does an AQI system provide, and how is it gathered (exercise Q.2h)?
blocks.explanation: Real-time and averaged concentrations of PM, NO2, SO2, CO, ozone and VOCs, converted into the index and its colour band for a place and time; the data come from fixed monitoring stations and continuous emission monitors on the ground and from satellite sensors covering wider regions.

items: CEMS at industrial sites; AQMS fixed stations in cities; satellite remote sensing over regions.
